actualMechanism: property-explorer-staging's CORTEX_API_URL resolves to the Cloud Run 'staging' TAG (https://staging---cortex-api-tds7av26va-uc.a.run.app), not to the untagged default URL. That tag pointed at an old revision (cortex-api-00646-luj, deployed 2026-08-28) which itself read a DIFFERENT secret (STAGING_DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL, not DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_DIRECT) bound to a dead Neon branch (ep-wispy-fire-apd2q819). This explains everything this lane measured: the old response SCHEMA (older code on 00646-luj, not a cache -- a warm instance cannot change a response schema, only different code can) and the old timestamp (a genuinely different, frozen DB branch). CP2/CP3's warm-instance-connection hypothesis is REFUTED by doc-repo-79's pre-registered test (moving the Cloud Run tag alone, zero Vercel change, fixed it instantly -- proves the tag was the variable, not instance warmth).
fix: doc-repo-79 repointed STAGING_DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL at the stable branch, deployed cortex-api-00747-yir from the current serving image with --no-traffic, and moved the 'staging' tag onto it. No Vercel project was touched. Verified live: property-explorer-staging now serves 16,466 bytes / snapshotAt 2026-09-01T22:43:35.532Z, matching production and cortex-api direct exactly. Production traffic never moved (cortex-api-00745-cud stayed 100%); smartsite.cloud untouched throughout.
correctionToThisLanesEarlierMeasurement: CP2 reported CORTEX_API_URL as an empty string on property-explorer-staging, based on `vercel env ls` / `vercel env pull`. That was wrong (or at least misleading) -- the real stored value is the staging tag URL. `vercel env pull`'s repeated inconsistency on this lane's own CORTEX_SERVICE_API_KEY pulls (non-empty on first pull, empty on a later pull, same var) in hindsight was a warning sign that pulled values for encrypted vars are not reliable evidence of the true stored value. Future lanes: don't trust `vercel env pull`/`env ls` output alone for an encrypted var when the question is load-bearing -- verify by observable behavior (like doc-repo-79's direct curl to the suspected real target) rather than by reading the config back through a tool that may not faithfully reveal it.
whatThisLaneGotRightAnyway: The STOP on the original dispatch's literal instruction (set STAGING_NEONDB_URL on smart-site-factory) was still correct -- that action genuinely would have been a no-op regardless of the CORTEX_API_URL question, since smart-site-factory itself has no DB-related code path at all. The isolation methodology (byte-count + fact-family presence, not just timestamp; testing property-explorer-staging directly to rule out the /site rewrite; testing production to bound the blast radius) is what let doc-repo-79 find and verify the real fix quickly -- per their own message, both instruments were reused directly.
